archetype.name: Game Manager (spot-start backup)
archetype.definition: A tall, pocket-bound backup who wins only on quick, short throws to the middle of the field, rarely pushes the ball, and needs the offense around him to supply the explosive plays.

report.headline: Accurate underneath, empty deep, and sacked too often to move an offense.
report.take:
Tanner McKee is a sixth-round backup who has played every snap of three games this season: starts in Weeks 6 and 8, plus Week 7, when Jalen Hurts was listed as the starter. The Eagles lost all three. His passing yards were almost identical each week (215, 211, 212), and that flatness tells you what he is. He takes what's in front of him, completes it at a slightly above-average clip (63.2% against a 62.2% league average), and rarely threatens anything past the sticks. His intended air yards sit at 6.82, and his average throw lands 2.84 yards short of the line to gain. That is a checkdown profile, and it explains a third-down conversion rate of 28.6% on an average of 9.4 yards to go.

The split by depth is the whole story. Short throws (0-9 air yards) are slightly positive at +0.066 EPA with a +4.0 CPOE. Intermediate throws are better than you'd expect at +0.207, though that rests on 20 attempts and a 50% completion rate. Throws over the middle have been his best area by a distance (+0.296 on 17 plays). Then come the extremes. He went 0-for-8 on deep balls with an interception, which cost 9.5 points by itself against a dropback total of -18.1. Throws behind the line, mostly screens and swings, cost another 4.7, largely through Elijah Mitchell, who sits at -0.427 EPA per target. Take away those two buckets and you have a roughly average short-area passer. Leave them in and you have the 42nd-ranked EPA per dropback out of 55 qualifiers.

The numbers also hide the sack problem, and the way he is adapting to it. He has taken 10 sacks at an 8.1% rate, and his 31.3% pressure-to-sack conversion ranks 26th of 45. That is a pace of 57 sacks over a full season. He doesn't escape much either, with five scrambles all year. Across his three games he became steadily more conservative: aggressiveness fell from 22.2% to 11.4% to 8.8%, and his CPOE rose each week to +2.9 at Washington. Even so, that Washington game was his worst by EPA (-9.5), because he took five sacks and lost a fumble. Playing safer has made him more accurate, but the offense has not moved better. His +6.7 CPOE while trailing by nine or more is soft-coverage padding. When the game was within one score, his CPOE was -7.5.

He is now listed as QB2, Joe Milton III has started the last two games, and McKee carries a rib injury. On a team whose offense ranks last in success rate, this looks like a capable emergency option, not a starter in waiting. His two prior one-game samples, one excellent in 2024 and one ordinary in 2025, are too thin to argue for a higher ceiling.

strengths.title: Clean short-to-middle accuracy
strengths.body: Inside 10 air yards he completes 73.5% of throws, four points over expected, and throws over the middle have been his most productive area. This is what a 6'6" pocket passer with a quick, defined read should do. It is the part of his game most likely to hold up, because it depends on timing rather than playmaking.

strengths.title: Accuracy improving game to game
strengths.body: His CPOE climbed each week, from -6.4 to -2.2 to +2.9, and his bad-throw rate is down from last season's 23.3%. Some of that comes from throwing shorter, but he looked more settled the more he played. This is a modest positive, not a breakout.

strengths.title: Finds Lemon and Goedert
strengths.body: His two most-targeted receivers, Makai Lemon and Dallas Goedert, are both positive per target. Throws to them are the most efficient part of his production. Keep the ball with those two and the offense functions; spread it to the back and the third receiver and it stalls.

concerns.title: No vertical game at all
concerns.body: He went 0-for-8 on throws of 20+ air yards with an interception, and those eight throws alone erased the gains from his short and intermediate work. The low aggressiveness and short intended air yards suggest this isn't bad luck on a few shots: he doesn't see or trust the deep window. Eight attempts is a small sample, but nothing in the profile argues it will flip.

concerns.title: Sacks swallow his drives
concerns.body: Ten sacks in three games, and nearly a third of his pressures ending in a sack, put him on a 57-sack pace. He doesn't extend plays to make up for it, scrambling on only 3.9% of dropbacks, so this isn't the cost of creativity. It reflects slow processing behind a line that ranks 23rd in hits allowed, and it is a real flaw.

concerns.title: Fades when the game is live
concerns.body: Within one score his CPOE is -7.5 and his success rate is 32.9%. His better accuracy numbers came while trailing by nine or more, against defenses guarding the sideline and conceding underneath. The box score flatters him in exactly the situations that matter least.

trend.note: His yardage barely moved across three games (215, 211, 212), and his EPA stayed negative every week. The only shift was stylistic: aggressiveness fell from 22.2% to 8.8% while accuracy rose, and sacks wiped out the gain.

nextGame.headline: Dallas leaks short passes, but he's QB2 with sore ribs
nextGame.body:
On paper this is the best possible matchup for his style. Dallas ranks last in defensive EPA and 28th against short passes (+0.185 EPA). Short passes are where McKee makes his living. The Cowboys are comparatively decent deep (8th), which doesn't matter to a passer who went 0-for-8 there. He has already seen this defense: Week 7 at home was his most efficient game (-3.2 EPA, 211 yards), and it still ended 21-38. As an 8.5-point underdog against Dallas's third-ranked offense, Philadelphia should be throwing from behind, so volume would be there.

The bigger question is whether he plays at all. He is listed QB2, Milton has started the last two games, and McKee is questionable with a rib injury on a four-day Thanksgiving turnaround. Ribs are a real concern for a quarterback taking 3.3 sacks a game. On his side, Goedert (shin) is questionable and Wicks is on injured reserve, which thins out his short-area targets. Dallas is missing a lot of its back seven: cornerback DaRon Bland (89% of snaps) is on injured reserve, safeties Jalen Thompson and P.J. Locke are out, and linebacker Jaishawn Barham is out. A depleted Cowboys secondary is exactly what a quick-game passer wants to see.

keyMatchups.title: Quick game vs. soft underneath
keyMatchups.body: Dallas allows +0.185 EPA on short throws, among the worst in the league, and gives up +0.42 per target to opposing WR1s. Quick throws to Lemon and the slot should be open all day, especially with Bland out. This is the one area where his strength meets their weakness.

keyMatchups.title: Running-back checkdowns go nowhere
keyMatchups.body: Dallas is second-stingiest against lead backs, at -0.2 EPA per play. McKee's targets to Elijah Mitchell already run at -0.427 EPA each. If pressure pushes him to dump it off, those plays will likely die, so the ball has to go to wideouts and Goedert.

keyMatchups.title: Pass rush vs. sore ribs
keyMatchups.body: Dallas sacks at a middle-of-the-pack 6.7% rate, but McKee turns pressure into sacks more often than most. With injured ribs, every hit carries extra risk, both to the drive and to whether he finishes the game.

nextGame.watch: Whether McKee is active and in the starting role at all. If he plays, watch whether he takes even one real shot downfield or lives entirely underneath.

restOfSeason.body:
As QB2 behind Milton, McKee's rest of season depends on someone else's health or struggles. If he does start, expect the same game: about 38 attempts, lots of short completions, few touchdowns, and a heavy sack load. Something like 195-235 passing yards a game, with touchdowns at the low end of the league. His 63% completion rate and short-area efficiency should hold. The red-zone TD rate (two touchdowns on six plays) and the strong CPOE while trailing are small or flattering samples and should cool. The deep 0-for-8 should improve slightly just through completions on occasional attempts, but not enough to change who he is.

The part most likely to stay is the sacks. A pressure-to-sack rate near the bottom third, behind a line that already allows plenty of hits, means 2.5 to 4 sacks a start remains a fair range. Without a vertical element, this offense will stay near the bottom of the league in success rate whenever he is under center.
swingFactors: Whether he regains the starting job from Milton
Rib injury and how it handles hits
Goedert's availability as a short-area target

confidence.note: 114 attempts across three games, now QB2, with a rib injury.
